items.stem: Time-to-fill is most usefully defined as the number of days from:

options.text: Job approval to the candidate's first day
options.rationale: That spans approval and onboarding; it mixes several processes.

options.text: Job posting (or requisition opening) to offer acceptance
options.rationale: Correct: a consistent start and end point makes time-to-fill comparable.
That measures only part of the interview stage.
That is notice period, not time-to-fill.

items.stem: The workforce gap is best described as the difference between:

options.text: Forecast demand and projected internal supply
options.rationale: Correct: the gap is future need minus the people you expect to have.

options.text: This year's budget and last year's budget
options.rationale: Budget change is not the workforce gap.
The org chart alone does not express future demand or supply.
Historical flows are inputs, not the gap itself.

items.explanation: Correct: the gap is future need minus the people you expect to have.

items.stem: Which TWO practices reduce the risk of misleading conclusions in people analytics? (Select TWO)

options.text: Checking for confounding variables before claiming a cause
options.rationale: Correct: confounders can create a false impression of cause.

options.text: Agreeing consistent metric definitions up front
options.rationale: Correct: shared definitions keep comparisons valid over time.

options.text: Reporting only the result that supports the plan
options.rationale: Cherry-picking results is a source of bias, not a safeguard.
Acting on every correlation invites spurious decisions.

items.explanation: Correct: confounders can create a false impression of cause.; Correct: shared definitions keep comparisons valid over time.
